title: Async WebSockets & Streaming in Python
summary: Covers real-time connections in asyncio Python. It walks through the WebSocket protocol, then websockets, aiohttp and FastAPI/Starlette endpoints. It also covers heartbeats, backpressure, broadcasting, reconnecting with backoff, close codes, and streaming with Server-Sent Events from async generators.

chapters.title: WebSocket Fundamentals: Handshake, Frames, Full Duplex
points: WebSocket (RFC 6455) = one long-lived, full-duplex TCP connection where client and server can each send at any time; ws:// runs on port 80, wss:// uses TLS on port 443
The handshake is a normal HTTP/1.1 GET with 'Upgrade: websocket', 'Connection: Upgrade', 'Sec-WebSocket-Key' and 'Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13'
The server replies '101 Switching Protocols' with Sec-WebSocket-Accept = base64(SHA1(key + fixed GUID)); after that the socket stops speaking HTTP
Frame opcodes: 0x0 continuation, 0x1 text (UTF-8), 0x2 binary, 0x8 close, 0x9 ping, 0xA pong; the last three are control frames
Client-to-server frames must be masked with a 4-byte key; server-to-client frames are unmasked
A message can be split across several frames (fragmentation); libraries reassemble them, so your code sees whole messages
Comparison: short polling (repeated requests), long polling (a held request per event), SSE (server-to-client only, over HTTP), WebSocket (two-way, low per-message overhead)
The asyncio model is one coroutine/task per connection; thousands of idle sockets cost only memory, not threads
Any blocking call (time.sleep, sync DB driver, CPU loop) freezes every connection in the event loop; offload it with asyncio.to_thread
Use WebSockets for chat, live collaboration, games and trading ticks; prefer SSE or plain HTTP when data only flows server → client

chapters.title: The websockets Library: Server and Client
points: Modern API: 'from websockets.asyncio.server import serve'; 'async with serve(handler, "", 8765) as server: await server.serve_forever()'
The handler takes one argument, 'async def handler(ws)'; the request path is in ws.request.path (the old (ws, path) signature was removed)
Receive loop: 'async for message in ws:'; it ends cleanly on a normal close and raises ConnectionClosedError on an abnormal one
'await ws.send(x)': str → text frame, bytes → binary frame; an iterable of chunks → a fragmented message
'await ws.recv()' reads a single message; it raises ConnectionClosedOK (codes 1000/1001) or ConnectionClosedError (anything else)
Client: 'from websockets.asyncio.client import connect'; 'async with connect("ws://host:8765") as ws:' closes the connection on exit
max_size defaults to 1 MiB; a larger incoming message closes the connection with 1009 (message too big)
To send and receive at the same time, run a reader task and a writer task under asyncio.TaskGroup
process_request(connection, request) hook: check auth headers or tokens and return an HTTP 401/403 response before the upgrade happens
Example: an echo server in 5 lines, 'async for m in ws: await ws.send(m)'

chapters.title: aiohttp WebSocket Server and Client
points: Server: 'ws = web.WebSocketResponse(heartbeat=30); await ws.prepare(request)', and the handler must finally 'return ws'
Receive loop: 'async for msg in ws:' then branch on msg.type: WSMsgType.TEXT / BINARY / ERROR (the loop stops on CLOSE)
Send helpers: send_str, send_bytes, send_json; receive helpers: receive_str, receive_json
Client: 'async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s: async with s.ws_connect(url, heartbeat=30) as ws:'; reuse the session and don't create one per connection
heartbeat=N sends a ping every N seconds and closes the connection if no pong arrives in time; autoping=True answers incoming pings for you
receive_timeout bounds each receive(); max_msg_size defaults to 4 MiB (0 = unlimited, which is dangerous)
Graceful shutdown: keep sockets in a weakref.WeakSet on the app and in on_shutdown call 'await ws.close(code=WSCloseCode.GOING_AWAY)'
Check ws.closed before sending; after the peer closes, sends raise ConnectionResetError
Comparison with websockets: aiohttp bundles an HTTP server and client plus WebSocket support; websockets is a focused, spec-strict WebSocket-only library

chapters.title: FastAPI / Starlette WebSocket Endpoints
points: '@app.websocket("/ws") async def ep(websocket: WebSocket):' then you must 'await websocket.accept()' before sending
Methods: receive_text / receive_bytes / receive_json and send_text / send_bytes / send_json; iterators: 'async for m in websocket.iter_text()'
A client disconnect raises WebSocketDisconnect (with a .code attribute); catch it to deregister the client in a finally/except block
Path and query params and Depends() work as they do in HTTP routes; browsers can't set headers on a WebSocket, so pass tokens in the query string or the first message
Reject auth before accepting: 'await websocket.close(code=status.WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION)' or raise WebSocketException; HTTPException does not apply
Uvicorn needs a WebSocket backend: install 'uvicorn[standard]' (websockets or wsproto) or the upgrade fails with a 404/warning
Receiving and pushing at once: TaskGroup with a recv task plus a send task that reads a per-client queue
With multiple workers (--workers 4) each process has its own set of connections; broadcasting across workers needs Redis or another broker
Testing: 'with TestClient(app).websocket_connect("/ws") as ws: ws.send_text(...); ws.receive_text()'

chapters.title: Ping/Pong Heartbeats and Keepalive
points: Why heartbeat: NATs, load balancers and proxies silently drop idle TCP connections, and a dead peer can go unnoticed for minutes
A ping frame (0x9) must be answered with a pong (0xA) carrying the same payload; an unsolicited pong acts as a one-way keepalive
websockets defaults: ping_interval=20, ping_timeout=20; with no pong, the connection closes with 1011 (keepalive ping timeout)
Manual ping in websockets: 'pong = await ws.ping(); latency = await pong' measures round-trip time
aiohttp: heartbeat=30 on WebSocketResponse and ws_connect; Uvicorn: --ws-ping-interval 20 --ws-ping-timeout 20
Browser JavaScript can't send protocol ping frames, so add app-level {'type':'ping'} messages if the client needs to detect dead links itself
Proxy idle timeouts, such as nginx proxy_read_timeout (default 60s), must be longer than the ping interval or the proxy cuts the connection
TCP keepalive (OS default about 2 hours) is far too slow to detect dead peers; use WebSocket-level pings
Trade-off: a shorter interval detects failures faster but costs more wakeups and traffic across 10k+ connections; 20–30s is typical

chapters.title: Backpressure and Bounded Queues
points: Backpressure: a slow consumer must slow down the producer; otherwise buffers grow without limit until the process runs out of memory
In websockets, 'await ws.send()' waits once the write buffer passes the high-water mark (write_limit, default 32 KiB); always await it
Receive side: websockets max_queue (default 16 messages); when it is full, the library stops reading and TCP flow control pushes back on the sender
Use asyncio.Queue(maxsize=N): 'await q.put(x)' blocks the producer when the queue is full; never use an unbounded Queue() on a hot path
put_nowait raises asyncio.QueueFull, which lets you pick a drop policy: drop newest, drop oldest (get_nowait then put), or disconnect the client
Choose a policy by data type: latest-value data (prices, cursors) → drop old or keep one slot; event logs/chat → block or disconnect with 1008/1013
Guard slow sends: 'await asyncio.wait_for(ws.send(m), timeout=5)', and close the client on timeout
Pattern: producer → bounded per-client queue → one writer task per client doing 'await ws.send(await q.get())'
Mistake: fire-and-forget create_task(ws.send()) for each message hides errors and discards backpressure

chapters.title: Broadcasting to Many Clients
points: Registry: a set of connections; 'clients.add(ws)' in try, 'clients.discard(ws)' in finally so disconnects never leak entries
Naive loop 'for ws in clients: await ws.send(m)' lets one slow client stall the whole broadcast
'asyncio.gather(*(ws.send(m) for ws in clients), return_exceptions=True)' sends concurrently, but the slowest client still sets the finish time
websockets.asyncio.server.broadcast(connections, message) is synchronous: it writes without waiting and skips clients that are closed or backed up
Robust pattern: put the message on every client's bounded queue and let each client's writer task apply its own drop/disconnect policy
Serialize once (json.dumps before the loop), not once per client; fan-out cost is O(N) writes per message
Iterate over a snapshot (list(clients)), because the set can change during an await and raise 'set changed size during iteration'
Multiple processes or hosts: publish to Redis pub/sub (redis.asyncio) or NATS, and each worker fans out to its local clients
Rooms/topics: dict[str, set[ws]] maps each topic to its subscribers; remove empty rooms to avoid leaks

chapters.title: Graceful Close Codes and Reconnect with Backoff
points: Close handshake: one side sends a close frame (code + reason ≤123 bytes), the other echoes it, then the server closes the TCP connection
Codes: 1000 normal, 1001 going away (shutdown/navigation), 1002 protocol error, 1003 unsupported data
More codes: 1008 policy violation (auth), 1009 message too big, 1011 internal error, 1012 service restart, 1013 try again later
1006 abnormal closure is never sent on the wire; it is a local report that the TCP connection died without a close frame
Codes 4000–4999 are for your application (e.g. 4001 token expired); send them with 'await ws.close(code=4001, reason="expired")'
Reconnect policy: retry on 1001/1006/1011/1012/1013; do not retry blindly on 1008 or 4xxx auth failures, fix credentials first
Exponential backoff with full jitter: 'delay = random.uniform(0, min(cap, base * 2**attempt))', which prevents a thundering herd after an outage
Reset the attempt counter only after the connection has stayed stable for a while, not right after the handshake
websockets: 'async for ws in connect(uri):' reconnects with built-in backoff; catch ConnectionClosed inside and 'continue'
After a reconnect, re-authenticate, re-subscribe and resume from the last seen message id so no events are lost

chapters.title: Server-Sent Events and Async Generator Streaming
points: SSE = a single HTTP response with 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' that stays open while the server pushes text events
Wire format: 'event:', 'data:', 'id:', 'retry:' lines, and a blank line ends each event; a line starting with ':' is a comment (use it as a heartbeat)
The browser EventSource reconnects automatically (after the retry: delay) and sends a 'Last-Event-ID' header so the server can resume
FastAPI: 'return StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type="text/event-stream")' where gen is an async generator yielding 'data: ...\n\n'
Detect disconnects: check 'await request.is_disconnected()' in the loop; cancellation raises CancelledError/GeneratorExit, so release resources in finally
The sse-starlette EventSourceResponse adds ping comments, disconnect handling and proper formatting
Proxies buffer by default: send 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' and 'Cache-Control: no-cache', and disable gzip for the stream
HTTP/1.1 browsers allow only 6 connections per domain, which caps open SSE tabs; HTTP/2 multiplexing removes this limit
SSE vs WebSocket: SSE is server → client only and text only, but it works through HTTP infrastructure and auth and reconnects by itself; it is the right choice for LLM token streams and notifications
aiohttp equivalent: 'resp = web.StreamResponse(); await resp.prepare(req); await resp.write(b"data: x\n\n")'

chapters.title: Cheatsheet: Async WebSockets & Streaming
points: Server one-liners: websockets 'serve(handler, host, port)' · aiohttp 'WebSocketResponse().prepare(req)' · FastAPI '@app.websocket' + accept()
Loops: 'async for m in ws' (websockets/aiohttp) · 'websocket.iter_text()' (Starlette); catch ConnectionClosed / WebSocketDisconnect
Keepalive: ping every 20–30s, timeout about 20s; keep proxy idle timeouts longer than the ping interval
Backpressure: always await send, use bounded asyncio.Queue(maxsize), give each consumer a drop/disconnect policy, and wrap sends in wait_for
Broadcast: registry set with a finally-block cleanup, per-client queue + writer task, serialize once, Redis pub/sub across workers
Close codes: 1000 ok · 1001 going away · 1006 dropped (local only) · 1008 policy · 1009 too big · 1011 error · 1012 restart · 4xxx app
Reconnect: exponential backoff with full jitter and a cap, no retry on auth failures, re-subscribe and resume from the last id
SSE: text/event-stream, 'data: ...\n\n', id + Last-Event-ID resume, ':' comment heartbeats, disable proxy buffering
Top mistakes: blocking calls in handlers, unbounded queues, sequential broadcast, forgetting accept(), no heartbeat behind a proxy
Pick one: two-way and low latency → WebSocket · server push over plain HTTP → SSE · rare updates → plain HTTP polling
